newsitem.title: USA: US shrs end mostly up, Dow off but rises for week.
newsitem.headline: US shrs end mostly up, Dow off but rises for week.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks edged lower on Friday as investors engaged in mild profit-taking after two straight sessions of solid gains.

The Dow fell 11 points to close unofficially at 6813. The decline shaved off only a small fraction of the index's gains for the week, which totaled about 117 points, or a little less than two percent.
Broader indicators showed continued strength. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite indices were both higher, and market breadth was mildly positive on both the NYSE and Nasdaq.

Bond prices jumped on the news, driving the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury down to 6.79 percent and triggering a rally in stocks that lost steam only in the final minutes of the session.

"Investors have been watching the yield on the long bond very carefully because many see seven percent as a level where stocks may give back ground," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
"We did see a little profit-taking at the end, but with yields a bit lower there's a sense it's best to stay the course," he said.

The so-called January Barometer -- which by the purest method actually tracks the S&P 500 -- calls for the market to finish the year higher when it rises in January and lower when it falls in the month.
According to data from the Hirsch Organization, the barometer has forecast the market's direction in 41 out of the last 46 years.
The S&P 500 finished the session at 786.16, up 1.99 for the day and up 45.42 points, or six percent, for the month.
Drug stocks remained strong. The American Stock Exchange Pharmaceutical Index .DRG rose 4.46 points to 397.73.
Warner-Lambert Co rose three to 81, Pfizer Inc gained 1-3/4 to 92-1/2 and Schering-Plough Corp climbed 1-5/8 to 72-1/8.
"The drug stocks continue to power up," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "They offer a classic defensive posture along with growth opportunity."
In individual issues, Mercury Finance Corp was the NYSE's most active stock, plummeting 12-7/8 to two on more than 35 million shares in volume.
